clue.text: Woos epigrammatist hence losses of commission?

parts.note: to woo a sweetheart is to court them
Martial was the Roman poet famed for his epigrams

explanation.surface: A suitor who writes witty verse pays the price in lost commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commission' looks like a salesman's fee, but it is an officer's rank: a military trial can strip an officer of it, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A military trial can end with an officer being cashiered, losing the rank granted by royal warrant.

clue.text: Put up an idle scrawl-do nothing that will arouse the somnolent

parts.note: to cock an ear or hat is to raise or put it up
an gives the article A
a doodle is an aimless scribble made idly
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone scribbles idly and does nothing, yet something will wake the sleepers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about laziness, but the sleepy ones are roused by a rooster's crow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster's crow at dawn is the traditional alarm that wakes sleepers.

clue.text: Putting together King Claudius' pearl

definitions.meaning: joining things together is a combination or merger
in Hamlet, Claudius drops a precious pearl, which he calls by this name, into the poisoned cup

explanation.definitionFit: Joining is a merger, and Shakespeare's Claudius uses the old word for a large fine pearl.

clue.text: Spelaean type of gold processed in Ilium (the "h is dropped)

indicators.note: in places the reworked gold within the city name

parts.note: Ilium is the Latin name of Troy

indicators.note: processed means the letters of gold are worked over into a new order
the clue says the h of the word before is dropped, as a Cockney would drop it

parts.note: taken as written before its letter is lost

explanation.surface: Gold is worked over in ancient Troy, with a note on dropping aitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges the gold inside the city of Ilium; the bracketed '"h is dropped' tells you to say 'the' without its aitch, the way a Cockney would.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelaean means cave-dwelling, and a cave-dweller is the classic sense of this word.

clue.text: Doctor is extremely young and wet

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
taken as written
ten years old is a very young age, so the number stands for a very young child

explanation.surface: A doctor who is still a child, and soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something is to make it a little wet, so 'wet' as a verb fits.

clue.text: About ten, possibly, about to return — to the stage

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of ten may be arranged another way
to return asks for this short word to be turned back to front

parts.note: re again means concerning

explanation.surface: Around ten, perhaps, an actor is about to go back on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TEN as ENT; 'to return' turns the second RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who comes back on to the boards does so after an exit, making a second appearance in the scene.

clue.text: Zulu warriors echo J. Horner's self-satisfaction

definitions.meaning: Little Jack Horner said 'What a good boy am I'

explanation.definitionFit: A Zulu regiment has this name, and split as I'M PI it is a smug claim to piety.

clue.text: Warden of Arden's running brooks?

parts.note: in As You Like It, the Forest of Arden has 'books in the running brooks', so a keeper of those books is meant

explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of books is in charge of a collection of volumes, here the books Shakespeare finds in Arden's streams.

clue.text: The harmony of letters

explanation.definitionFit: Agreement between things and the mail people exchange share one word.

clue.text: Outstandingly feminine attire

parts.note: a woman's garment that literally stands out, held wide by a stiff frame

explanation.definitionFit: This is a stiff petticoat that held Victorian skirts out wide.

clue.text: One of this name was periodically blue

definitions.text: One of this name was periodically blue

parts.words: One of this name was periodically blue
parts.note: the painter Picasso, who bore this first name, had a Blue Period

explanation.definitionFit: Picasso's first name, and his Blue Period was a phase of sad blue paintings.

clue.text: Cancel a turn by Sally

indicators.note: a turn here turns the bun's name round so it reads from the far end

parts.note: a Sally Lunn is a sweet bun from Bath, so Sally calls up LUNN

explanation.surface: Sally takes her turn and calls the whole thing off.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sally Lunn is a light teacake from Bath, England; 'turn' reverses LUNN to NNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, which is to cancel.

clue.text: Carry to a better place ?

definitions.meaning: the totalisator, where a punter or 'better' places a bet

explanation.definitionFit: To lug something is to tote it, and the racecourse totalisator is where a punter goes to bet.

clue.text: Henry's fishwife

parts.note: Henry VIII's sixth wife was Catherine, whose surname is also a young salmon

explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's last queen, and a parr is a young salmon.

clue.text: Somewhat rough journal that is ready to impart polish

definitions.text: Somewhat rough journal that is ready to impart polish

parts.words: Somewhat rough journal that is ready to impart polish
parts.note: the 'journal' is a sheet of abrasive-coated paper, rough enough to polish

explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive grit glued to a sheet, used to smooth and polish surfaces.

clue.text: Townsman gives work to virtuous lion-tamer

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
pi is slang for pious
Daniel survived the lions' den, so a short form of his name stands for him

explanation.surface: A local man hires a saintly lion-tamer.
explanation.walkthrough: An OPPIDAN is an Eton schoolboy who boards in the town, or any town-dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin oppidum, a town, the word means a town-dweller.

clue.text: First man of action

parts.note: the person who brings a lawsuit, an action, is the first party named

explanation.definitionFit: The person who starts a lawsuit is the one who sues.

clue.text: What's left of the new seminar ?

indicators.note: new says the letters of seminar are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: What survives of the seminar after it has been redone.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers or the rest of something are what is left.

clue.text: Pack-member holds its reversal to be severe

indicators.note: reversal says the whole combination is read backwards
holds means the short word sits inside the pack member

parts.note: a card is a member of a pack

explanation.surface: A dog in the pack holds back its own retreat, harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack-member' suggests a wolf or hound, but the pack is of playing cards; 'holds' and 'reversal' then act on the card and 'its' together.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme, harsh or severe ones.

clue.text: Composer on origin of Elizabethan shoe-style

parts.note: Chopin was the Polish composer

indicators.note: origin of points to the opening letter of Elizabethan

explanation.surface: A composer discusses the beginnings of Tudor footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHOPINE is a tall platform shoe worn in the 16th and 17th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopine was a high platform overshoe of Renaissance fashion.

clue.text: Spanish bull not uncommonly found in Canada

parts.note: toro is Spanish for bull

indicators.note: uncommonly means the letters of not are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A Spanish bull turns up in Canada, which is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario's capital is a city located in Canada.

clue.text: Traumatic transport for a poor clock-watcher

definitions.text: Traumatic transport for a poor clock-watcher

parts.words: Traumatic transport for a poor clock-watcher
parts.note: the passenger watches the meter's clock tick up the fare, painful if poor

explanation.definitionFit: A hired car with a fare meter, an alarming sight for someone short of cash.

clue.text: Long time, no see ? Not quite, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the remaining letters might be arranged otherwise
not quite means the phrase stops one letter short of its end

explanation.surface: An old friend greeted after an age, with some hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last E of NOSEE, leaving NOSE; 'perhaps' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeons are ages, immeasurably long periods.

clue.text: How 'to persuade the firm — with a kiss

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A tip on winning over a company: seal it with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle someone gently is to win them over by persuasion.

clue.text: Took steps to reveal fake diamonds, say

indicators.note: say indicates that the word for fake gems is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: paste is the glass used to make imitation gems

explanation.surface: A jeweller walked about to expose some bogus stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Walked with measured strides, taking one step after another.

clue.text: Indiaman

parts.note: read as 'India man', the 18th-century general known as 'of India'

explanation.definitionFit: Robert, Lord of Plassey, won Bengal for Britain and is remembered as the man of India.

clue.text: Daisy's wedding ring

parts.note: the song 'Daisy, Daisy' is about a girl with this surname, and wedding chimes ring

explanation.definitionFit: Church chimes peal at weddings, and the song 'Daisy, Daisy' is titled after her full name.

clue.text: Beggar's arch plea ?

parts.note: a beggar pleads '...!', and run together that is a pointed arch

explanation.definitionFit: A pointed Gothic arch or rib, which split in two sounds like a beggar's cry.

clue.text: Starting in top? Nice mess !

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bewildered newcomer starts at the top of a jumbled French resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A commencement or beginning is the point of starting.

clue.text: Crazy rustic meeting-place of Mistinguett and her Chevalier

definitions.text: meeting-place of Mistinguett and her Chevalier

parts.note: folies is French for follies or madness
a bergère is a French shepherdess, a country girl

explanation.surface: A mad country dance hall where a star and her lover met.
explanation.walkthrough: Mistinguett was a French music-hall star and Maurice Chevalier her partner; they performed at this Paris music hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Paris music hall where the singer Mistinguett and Maurice Chevalier performed together.
